prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a new original Wildbound cavern environment concept, landscape composition, at the artistic quality described by the user's attached pixel-art references. These references are art-direction references only, not scenes to copy: the top-down mossy ruins establishes navigable game-camera readability; the forest branch, waterfall ruins, swamp dock, snowy rock arch and bridge establish confident angular pixel clusters, large sculpted organic forms, deliberate material shading, deep foreground/midground separation and restrained atmospheric perspective; the dark teal fantasy scene establishes luminous focal accents within rich shadows.

Show a cohesive, explorable natural underground cave: two irregular connected limestone chambers with a winding, clearly walkable passage between them, viewed from a high three-quarter overhead action-RPG camera, orthographic with no horizon. Substantial tall fractured rock walls and eroded overhangs occupy the back and sides, with deep dark inaccessible rock beyond. NO flat outlined blobs or floating board-game islands. The floor is solid excavated bedrock with uneven shelves, damp seams, subtle sediment and readable open walking space. Left chamber contains an irregular underground teal pool fed by a narrow trickle falling down a wall; right chamber features restrained cyan crystal veins visibly embedded in fissures and a few mineable crystals growing from wall bases. Include asymmetric mineral columns and stalagmites grounded in calcite deposits, sparse pale mushrooms in moist recesses, small dark connecting tunnels disappearing behind rock, one narrow natural stone crossing over a water channel. A small original adventurer with a lantern provides scale, only about 5 percent of image height. One very subtle dust fall and small floor shadow in a side passage suggests a hidden ceiling hazard; do not expose overhead stalactites across the entire walkable floor. Visible decorative stalactites can frame remote high ledges.

Art direction: hand-crafted high-end pixel-art environment illustration, deliberate crisp square-pixel clusters, consistent pixel density, carefully placed stepped silhouettes, angular interlocking rock planes, grouped detail, blue-charcoal shadows, muted mineral greys with warm limestone lit faces, oxidized teal water, small pale cyan crystal highlights, subdued warm amber lantern accent. Sophisticated localized light with stepped color bands and luminous reflected water, never airbrushed or photoreal. Rich detail concentrated on rock planes and wet edges; keep walkable floor calmer. The rock mass should feel ancient, weighty, enclosed and geological, not generic repeated spikes or simple rounded platform shapes. A compelling composition with a clear entrance-to-chamber-to-tunnel path and strong depth, not an asset sheet, not a miniature tabletop diorama. Original arrangement, no copied architecture or characters. No text, labels, UI, borders or watermark. This is concept art to guide later editable game implementation, not a screenshot of an existing implementation.

Create a second, gameplay-oriented cavern concept using the supplied images as references. Image 1 is the initial cavern concept: preserve its idea of tall eroded rock, connected chambers, a flowing underground pool, wall crystals and a readable route, but redesign its camera and rendering. Images 2 and 3 are the user's primary PIXEL ART STANDARD: match their visibly chunky flat-color pixel clusters, restrained palettes, organized highlights, clean stepped contours, and confident large material shapes. Do NOT copy their outdoor architecture or characters. The previous cavern is too finely stippled and painterly. Simplify clusters substantially toward images 2 and 3; do not just downsample.

New original cavern composition, landscape: a higher three-quarter overhead orthographic action RPG view that shows the floor clearly, with one large underground pool chamber on the left and a second mineable-crystal chamber on the right, joined by a naturally bent rocky passage across the middle. A smaller tunnel branches upward through a dark archway. Massive natural limestone walls enclose the rooms with irregular black rock beyond, readable vertical faces and overlapping projecting rock shelves. Jagged slate and warm grey limestone planes, mineral streaks, a few irregular stalagmites rooted into calcite shelves, a small trickling waterfall into deep teal water with clear shallow margin and sparse stepped reflection marks. Crystals embedded into wall fissures with very restrained cyan reflected light. One tiny original adventurer for scale, 32 to 40 logical pixels tall, on a clear walkable floor. Small mushrooms near damp wall feet, grouped rubble away from the route. Only one subtle dust fall and floor shadow in a side alcove, representing a hidden ceiling hazard. No rows of hanging spikes over the path.

Use a consistent logical pixel grid roughly equivalent to a 640x420 pixel painting enlarged cleanly, not thousands of painterly specks. Broad shadows, controlled highlight clusters, selective detail, quiet floor shapes; reference-level hand-crafted pixel art with strong depth. Avoid all-over tessellated floor noise, 3D voxel appearance, gradients, soft brushwork, perfectly circular rooms, uniformly outlined room borders, isolated floating platforms, copied previous rejected cave mockups. No text, labels, UI, panels or watermark. This is a visual target for editable native game assets, not an implemented game screenshot.
